people.name: Paul Molitor
people.extract: Paul Leo Molitor, nicknamed "Mollie" and "the Ignitor", is an American former professional baseball player and manager. During his 21-year playing career in Major League Baseball (MLB), he played for the Milwaukee Brewers (1978–1992), Toronto Blue Jays (1993–1995), and Minnesota Twins (1996–1998). He was known for his exceptional hitting and speed. He made seven All-Star Game appearances, and was the World Series Most Valuable Player in 1993. Molitor ranks tenth on the all-time MLB career hits list with 3,319. He is one of only five players in history with 3,000+ hits, a lifetime .300+ batting average, and 500+ career stolen bases.
highlights: World Series Most Valuable Player in 1993.
Ranks tenth on all-time MLB career hits list.
One of five players with 3,000+ hits, .300+ average.

people.name: Archibald Willard
people.extract: Archibald MacNeal Willard was an American painter who was born and raised in Bedford, Ohio. His most famous work is "The Spirit of '76".
highlights: Famous for his work "The Spirit of '76".

people.name: Olli Määttä
people.extract: Olli Määttä is a Finnish professional ice hockey player who is a defenceman for the Minnesota Wild of the National Hockey League (NHL). He was drafted in the first round, 22nd overall, by the Pittsburgh Penguins in the 2012 NHL entry draft. Määttä has also played for the Chicago Blackhawks, Los Angeles Kings, Detroit Red Wings, Utah Mammoth, and Calgary Flames.
highlights: Drafted 22nd overall by Pittsburgh Penguins in 2012.
